bib.title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate

question: Can several LLM instances that propose answers then critique each other over rounds produce more accurate reasoning and fewer hallucinations than a single instance?
hypothesis: Multiagent debate (multiple agents, multiple rounds) improves reasoning and factuality over single-agent prompting, reflection and majority voting.
contributions: A multiagent debate procedure improving factual correctness and reasoning accuracy using only black-box access
A new benchmark of factual correctness: biographies of computer scientists
Evaluation over number of agents, rounds of debate and prompts across six tasks

method.summary: N copies of gpt-3.5-turbo each answer a question independently; each then receives the other agents' answers concatenated into a consensus prompt and updates its answer, repeated for R rounds. Compared to single agent, self-reflection and majority voting under identical starting prompts.
method.task: reasoning (arithmetic, GSM8K, chess move) and factuality (biographies, MMLU, chess validity)

datasets.name: Chess move prediction
datasets.source: pgnmentor.com Adams.zip; first 14 moves in PGN

datasets.name: MMLU
datasets.source: Hendrycks et al. 2020; randomly across subject areas

other.use: 20 GSM8K problems, mixed debate with chatGPT

inference.samples: main tables: 3 agents, 2 rounds; no number of runs or seeds stated
inference.prompting: zero-shot; same starting and debate prompt template across tasks (Fig 15); zero-shot chain of thought combined

parameters.summarization: used for more than 3 agents, by chatGPT

other.chess scoring: relative Stockfish pawn score, search depth 20

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: final answer correct (arithmetic, GSM8K boxed answer, MMLU letter)

metrics.name: Chess delta PS
metrics.definition: relative Stockfish pawn score after the suggested move

metrics.name: Biography accuracy
metrics.definition: percent of ground-truth bullets that chatGPT judges consistent (yes/no) with generated biography; 'uncertain' ignored

eval.protocol: ± values in Tables 1 and 2 are printed but the paper does not say what they are (std error?) ; ChatGPT used as judge for biographies; no cost or token counts reported

availability.data: biographies benchmark introduced; release not stated in text

prompts.text: Can you solve the following math problem? <Problem> Explain your reasoning. Your final answer should be a single numerical number, in the form \boxed{answer}, at the end of your response.

These are the solutions to the problem from other agents: <other agent responses> Using the solutions from other agents as additional information, can you provide your answer to the math problem? The original math problem is <Problem>. Your final answer should be a single numerical number, in the form \boxed{answer}, at the end of your response.

Here are some bullet point biographies of <person> given by other agents: <other agent response> Closely examine your biography and the biography of other agents and provide an updated bullet point biography.
These are the solutions to the problem from other agents: [other answers] Based off the opinion of other agents, can you give an updated response . . .
These are the solutions to the problem from other agents: [other answers] Using the opinion of other agents as additional advice, can you give an updated response . . .

evidence.quote: We run all experiments using the gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 model.

results.claim: Debate raises arithmetic accuracy from 67.0 to 81.8 over a single agent.
results.setup: gpt-3.5-turbo-0301, zero-shot, 3 agents, 2 debate rounds, same starting prompt as baselines; 100 generated six-number expressions

results.claim: Debate raises GSM8K accuracy from 77.0 to 85.0.
results.setup: gpt-3.5-turbo-0301, zero-shot, 3 agents, 2 debate rounds, same starting prompt as baselines; 100 GSM8K problems
results.table: Table 1, row Multi-Agent (Debate), column Grade School Math (%)

results.claim: Debate raises chess move quality (relative Stockfish pawn score) from 91.4 to 122.9.
results.setup: gpt-3.5-turbo-0301, zero-shot, 3 agents, 2 debate rounds, same starting prompt as baselines; 300 games, white move 14, Stockfish depth 20

results.claim: Majority voting over 3 agents gives a smaller gain than debate on GSM8K (81.0 vs 85.0).
results.setup: gpt-3.5-turbo-0301, zero-shot, 3 agents, 2 debate rounds, same starting prompt as baselines; majority baseline, same agent count
results.table: Table 1, row Multi-Agent (Majority), column Grade School Math (%)

results.claim: Majority voting gives only 69.0 on arithmetic vs 81.8 for debate.
results.setup: gpt-3.5-turbo-0301, zero-shot, 3 agents, 2 debate rounds, same starting prompt as baselines; majority baseline

results.claim: Self-reflection with a single agent lowers GSM8K accuracy (75.0 vs 77.0 single agent) though it helps arithmetic (72.1).
results.table: Table 1, row Single Agent (Reflection), column Grade School Math (%)

results.claim: Debate raises biography factual accuracy from 66.0 to 73.8.
results.setup: gpt-3.5-turbo-0301, 3 agents, 2 rounds; 524 computer scientists; ChatGPT judge yes/no vs Wikipedia bullet

results.claim: Debate raises MMLU accuracy from 63.9 to 71.1 while reflection lowers it to 57.7.
results.setup: gpt-3.5-turbo-0301, 3 agents, 2 rounds; 100 random MMLU questions
results.note: Reflection row is 57.7, below single agent 63.9

results.claim: Debate raises chess move validity from 29.3 to 45.2.
results.setup: gpt-3.5-turbo-0301, 3 agents, 2 rounds; BIG-Bench synthetic_short; 100 tasks
results.table: Table 2, row Multi-Agent (Debate), column Chess Move Validity

results.claim: Mixed ChatGPT and Bard debate solves 17 of 20 GSM8K problems vs 14 (ChatGPT) and 11 (Bard) alone.
results.note: Full sentence: Bard 11, chatGPT 14, joint debate 17 (p9). Tiny sample (20).

results.claim: Different persona initialization prompts raise MMLU debate accuracy from 71.1 to 74.2.
results.setup: persona prompts (professor, doctor, mathematician) per agent, MMLU
results.quote: improved performance on MMLU from 71.1 to 74.2 with different agents

results.claim: Arithmetic performance rises monotonically with number of agents (fixed 2 rounds); beyond 3 agents responses are summarised by ChatGPT, which improves over concatenation.
results.setup: Arithmetic; Fig 10a and Fig 13 (values only in figures)

results.claim: Arithmetic performance rises with debate rounds but rounds above four match four rounds.
Longer 'stubborn' prompts give slower convergence but better final answers than short prompts.
Debate cost scales with agents times rounds, and later rounds are dominated by recent context; converged answers can still be wrong.

limits: More expensive: multiple generations per round, times agents and rounds; no cost or token numbers given
Long debates: models focus on the most recent generations and struggle with long debate input
Converged answers are not necessarily correct; models confidently affirm wrong consensus
Small eval sets (100 items for most tasks); mixed-model test only 20 problems; error bars unexplained
Only gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 in main results; majority baseline omitted for factuality tasks; biography metric uses ChatGPT as judge and cannot catch facts outside ground truth
Agents are 'agreeable' (instruction tuning); no ablation holding total compute fixed against more majority samples beyond 3 agents
The PDF is arXiv v1 marked 'Preprint. Under review'; the caller's ICML 2024 venue is not in this text
